```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(tidyverse)
```

# Data Import
```{r}
NC_Spatial <- st_read("/Users/huangyiping/KalsiGivensHuangYang/data/raw_large/NC_wui_block_1990_2020_change_v4.shp")
NC_map <- counties(state = "NC", cb = TRUE)
```

# Data Info and Value Selection
```{r}
dim(NC_Spatial)
names(NC_Spatial)
```
## Interpretation

This dataset contains 266414 rows and 35 columns. For comparison between years, only six variables with data in both 2010 and 2020 or in 2011 and 2019 are selected: HU2010, HU2020, HUDEN2010, HUDEN2020, VEG2011PC, VEG2019PC.

# Missing Value Assessment
```{r}
missing_count=colSums(is.na(NC_Spatial))
missing_percent=colMeans(is.na(NC_Spatial)) * 100
missing_summary <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(NC_Spatial),
  Missing_Count = missing_count,
  Missing_Percent = round(missing_percent, 2)
)
missing_summary
```
## Interpretation 

No missing values across all variables.

# 3. Duplicate Observations

```{r}
nrow(NC_Spatial)
length(unique(NC_Spatial$BLK20))
sum(duplicated(NC_Spatial$BLK20))
sum(duplicated(NC_Spatial))
```
## Interpretation 

There is duplication on Block codes, due to the separated assessment between land and water region of a block. However, since none of the two rows have exact same values, the duplication would not cause problems for analysis. 

# Data Wrangling
```{r}
NC_Spatial_county <- NC_Spatial %>% 
  select(BLK20, HU2010, HU2020, HUDEN2010, HUDEN2020, VEG2011PC, VEG2019PC, geometry) %>%
  mutate(BLK20 = str_sub(BLK20, start = 1, end = 5)) %>%
  rename("County" = BLK20) %>%
  group_by(County) %>%
  summarise(HU2010 = sum(HU2010),
            HU2020 = sum(HU2020),
            HUDEN2010 = sum(HUDEN2010),
            HUDEN2020 = sum(HUDEN2020),
            VEG2011PC = sum(VEG2011PC),
            VEG2019PC = sum(VEG2019PC),
            geometry = st_union(geometry)) %>%
  mutate(HU_dif = HU2020-HU2010,
         HUDEN_dif = HUDEN2020-HUDEN2010,
         VEG_dif = VEG2019PC-VEG2011PC)
```

# Data Join

## Before Join
```{r}
dim(NC_map)
names(NC_map)
dim(NC_Spatial_county)
names(NC_Spatial_county)
```

### Interpretation

Before data join, NC_map has 100 rows and 13 columns. NC_Spatial_county has 100 rows and 11 columns. The two datasets will be joined by the county codes (GEOID column from NC_map and County column from NC_Spatial_county).

```{r}
NC_map_joined <- NC_map %>%
  mutate(GEOID = as.character(GEOID)) %>% 
  left_join(as.data.frame(NC_Spatial_county), 
    by = c("GEOID" = "County"))
```

## After Join
```{r}
dim(NC_map_joined)
names(NC_map_joined)
```

### Interpretation

Before data joining, NC_map_joined has 100 rows and 23 columns, which matches up with the original two datasets.

# Processed Data Export
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
dir.create("data/processed", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
st_write(
  NC_map_joined,
  "/Users/huangyiping/KalsiGivensHuangYang/data/processed/NC_map_joined.shp")
```
